inputs.question: How often must a high-risk CIB client's KYC be refreshed?

expected_facts: High-risk clients are refreshed every 12 months
expectations.reference_answer: High-risk clients must have their KYC refreshed every 12 months under the Global CDD Policy v2025.1.

inputs.question: What ownership threshold defines an ultimate beneficial owner under Meridian's global standard?

expected_facts: The UBO threshold is 25% ownership or control
Persons exercising control otherwise are also UBOs
expectations.reference_answer: Any natural person holding 25% or more ownership or control, or otherwise exercising control, is a UBO.

inputs.question: Within what timeframe must a potential sanctions match be dispositioned?

expected_facts: Potential matches must be dispositioned within 24 hours
expectations.reference_answer: Potential sanctions matches must be dispositioned within 24 hours.

inputs.question: What is the internal target for examining documents presented under a documentary credit?

expected_facts: The internal examination target is 3 banking days
expectations.reference_answer: Meridian's internal target is 3 banking days, inside the 5-banking-day maximum under international rules.

inputs.question: What is the maximum tenor for a usance LC before Credit Committee approval is needed?

expected_facts: Maximum usance LC tenor is 360 days
Longer tenors require Credit Committee approval
expectations.reference_answer: The maximum usance LC tenor is 360 days; anything longer needs Credit Committee approval.

inputs.question: What is the first-time-right target for onboarding and how is it defined?

expected_facts: The FTR target is 85%
FTR means approved with no rework loop back to the RM
expectations.reference_answer: The FTR target is 85%. A case is first-time-right when it is approved with no rework loop back to the RM.

inputs.question: How quickly should a client account be activated after KYC approval?

expected_facts: Accounts are activated within 1 business day of KYC approval
expectations.reference_answer: Accounts are activated within 1 business day of KYC approval.

inputs.question: How old can a proof of address document be at onboarding?

expected_facts: Proof of address must be no more than 3 months old
expectations.reference_answer: Proof of address must be no more than 3 months old.

inputs.question: Who can approve a waiver of discrepancies on an LC for USD 4 million?

expected_facts: A USD 4m waiver is approved by the Country Head of Trade Operations
Applicant written consent is required
expectations.reference_answer: The Country Head of Trade Operations (over USD 1m up to 5m band, matrix v2025.1). The applicant's written consent is also required.

inputs.question: Who approves a discrepancy waiver on a USD 12 million LC?

expected_facts: A USD 12m waiver is approved by the Regional Head of Trade Operations
Credit Risk concurrence is required
expectations.reference_answer: The Regional Head of Trade Operations, with Credit Risk concurrence (over USD 5m up to 20m band).

inputs.question: What is the KYC refresh cycle for a low-risk client?

expected_facts: Low-risk clients are refreshed every 36 months
expectations.reference_answer: Low-risk clients are refreshed every 36 months under the current policy.

inputs.question: What risk score range corresponds to a medium-risk rating?

expected_facts: Medium risk corresponds to a score of 41 to 70
expectations.reference_answer: Medium risk is a score of 41 to 70 on the 1-100 scale.

inputs.question: Under supply chain finance, what share of invoice value can be financed and for how long?

expected_facts: Up to 90% of approved invoice value can be financed
Maximum tenor is 180 days
expectations.reference_answer: Up to 90% of approved invoice value, for a maximum tenor of 180 days, for buyers graded 1-6.

inputs.question: Which approval body is required for a USD 60 million trade line?

expected_facts: A USD 60m trade line requires Regional Credit Committee approval
expectations.reference_answer: The Regional Credit Committee (over USD 25m up to 100m band).

inputs.question: What was the medium-risk KYC refresh cycle before the 2025 policy update?

expected_facts: Before March 2025 medium-risk refresh was 36 months
The current medium-risk refresh is 24 months
expectations.reference_answer: Before 1 March 2025 (policy v2024.1), medium-risk clients were refreshed every 36 months. It is now 24 months.

expected_facts: Medium-risk clients are refreshed every 24 months
Hong Kong medium-risk clients are refreshed every 18 months
expectations.reference_answer: Every 24 months under the current global policy, except Hong Kong where it is 18 months. Note the RM FAQ still says three years, which is outdated.

inputs.question: When did the revised trade discrepancy waiver thresholds take effect?

expected_facts: The revised waiver thresholds took effect on 1 April 2025
expectations.reference_answer: The revised waiver matrix (v2025.1) took effect on 1 April 2025.

inputs.question: What changed in the KYC refresh cycles in the 2025 policy?

expected_facts: Medium-risk changed from 36 to 24 months
Low-risk changed from 60 to 36 months
High-risk remained 12 months
expectations.reference_answer: Medium-risk moved from 36 to 24 months and low-risk from 60 to 36 months; high-risk stayed at 12 months.

inputs.question: Is a 9-month refresh cycle for high-risk clients now in effect?

expected_facts: The current high-risk refresh is 12 months
A 9-month cycle is not in effect
expectations.reference_answer: No. The current policy requires a 12-month refresh for high-risk clients. No approved policy sets a 9-month cycle.

inputs.question: What is the UBO threshold for a high-risk client in Singapore?

expected_facts: The Singapore UBO threshold for high-risk clients is 10%
expectations.reference_answer: 10% for high-risk clients in Singapore, lower than the global 25%.

inputs.question: How often are medium-risk clients in Hong Kong refreshed?

expected_facts: Hong Kong medium-risk clients are refreshed every 18 months
expectations.reference_answer: Every 18 months under the Hong Kong addendum, which overrides the global 24 months.

inputs.question: Who can certify corporate documents for a Hong Kong onboarding, and which documents?

expected_facts: Certified true copies of the Business Registration Certificate and Certificate of Incorporation are required
Certification can be by MGB staff, a certified public accountant or a solicitor
expectations.reference_answer: Certified true copies of the Business Registration Certificate and Certificate of Incorporation, certified by MGB staff, a CPA or a solicitor.

inputs.question: What additional review applies to a cash-intensive client in a UAE free zone?

expected_facts: Cash-intensive UAE free-zone entities are High risk by default
A transaction activity review is required every 6 months
expectations.reference_answer: It is High risk by default, with a transaction activity review every 6 months on top of the 12-month KYC refresh.

inputs.question: How much validity must a UAE trade licence have left at onboarding?

expected_facts: A UAE trade licence needs at least 90 days remaining validity
expectations.reference_answer: At least 90 days of remaining validity.

inputs.question: What must happen if a UK client's Companies House PSC register doesn't match the ownership they gave us?

expected_facts: The discrepancy must be reported to Onboarding Compliance
Reporting must happen within 5 business days
expectations.reference_answer: Report the discrepancy to Onboarding Compliance within 5 business days.

inputs.question: Do we need SoW and SoF for an EDD case with a four-layer ownership structure?

expected_facts: More than three ownership layers triggers EDD
EDD requires source of wealth and source of funds evidence
expectations.reference_answer: Yes. More than three ownership layers triggers EDD, and EDD requires source of wealth and source of funds evidence, plus dual approval.

inputs.question: Who signs off on onboarding a foreign PEP?

expected_facts: Foreign PEP onboarding is approved by the Group Head of Financial Crime Compliance
expectations.reference_answer: The Group Head of Financial Crime Compliance (FCC).

inputs.question: What's the TAT SLA for a high-risk onboarding and when does the clock start?

expected_facts: High-risk onboarding TAT is 20 business days
The clock starts when a complete document pack is received
The clock pauses while awaiting client information
expectations.reference_answer: 20 business days. The clock starts when a complete document pack is received and pauses while awaiting client information.

inputs.question: What approvals does an SBLC with an evergreen clause need?

expected_facts: Evergreen clauses require Legal and Credit approval
Final expiry must be no more than 5 years
expectations.reference_answer: Legal and Credit approval, with a final expiry no later than 5 years.

inputs.question: If I spot TBML indicators like over-invoicing on an LC, what's the threshold and when do I raise a UAR?

expected_facts: Invoice price variance over 25% from benchmark is a red flag
A UAR must be raised to FCC within 1 business day
expectations.reference_answer: A price variance over 25% from benchmark is a red flag. Raise a UAR to FCC within 1 business day.

inputs.question: A USD 8m LC has discrepancies and the applicant wants to waive them. Who approves the waiver and who gives the credit concurrence?

expected_facts: The Regional Head of Trade Operations approves the waiver
Credit concurrence comes from the Senior Credit Officer covering the client
Applicant written consent is required
expectations.reference_answer: The Regional Head of Trade Operations approves (over 5m to 20m band), with Credit Risk concurrence from the Senior Credit Officer covering the client. The applicant's written consent is required.

inputs.question: A medium-risk Hong Kong corporate gets an adverse media hit. When is its next KYC review due?

expected_facts: Adverse media is a trigger event
An out-of-cycle review is due within 30 calendar days
expectations.reference_answer: An adverse media hit is a trigger event, so an out-of-cycle review is due within 30 calendar days, regardless of the normal 18-month Hong Kong cycle.

inputs.question: A Singapore company owned by a domestic PEP is rated high risk. Who must approve onboarding and what UBO threshold applies?

expected_facts: The Country Head of Compliance approves the domestic PEP
EDD requires dual approval by the Country Head of Compliance and Country Head of CIB
The UBO threshold is 10%
expectations.reference_answer: PEP involvement and high risk trigger EDD, requiring dual approval by the Country Head of Compliance and the Country Head of CIB (the Country Head of Compliance also covers the domestic PEP approval). The UBO threshold is 10% in Singapore for high-risk clients.

inputs.question: An LC names a vessel with a three-day AIS gap and there is a port discrepancy in the documents. Can Trade Ops waive it?

expected_facts: Discrepancies in sanctions-relevant data such as ports cannot be waived
An AIS gap over 24 hours is a red flag
The case must be escalated to Sanctions
expectations.reference_answer: No. A port discrepancy is sanctions-relevant data, which cannot be waived, and an AIS gap over 24 hours is a red flag. Both must be escalated to Sanctions.

inputs.question: A prospective client has bearer shares that are not immobilised. Can we onboard them?

expected_facts: Bearer shares are prohibited unless immobilised with an approved custodian
expectations.reference_answer: No. Bearer shares are prohibited unless immobilised with an MGB-approved custodian.

expectations.reference_answer: Out of scope. The copilot covers CIB onboarding and trade operations policy, not HR or expense policy.
